key_insight: EVENET learns reusable patterns from simulated particle collisions and transfers them to multiple analysis tasks. Its ability to work on real collider data connects simulation-based training with experimental use.
problem_solved: Particle collision analysis needs models that can support different tasks and remain useful when moving from simulated events to real experimental data.
method: Pretrain a foundation model, EVENET, on simulated particle collisions.
Combine self-supervised learning with training guided by physics labels.
Transfer the pretrained model across analysis tasks and apply it to real collider data.
impact: EVENET demonstrates how foundation-model pretraining can support scientific analysis beyond language and images. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights the potential of combining self-supervision with domain-specific labels to learn transferable representations.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: simulated collisions → hybrid pretraining → EVENET → downstream analysis tasks.
Two-stream training graphic showing self-supervised learning and physics labels feeding one model.
Hub-and-spoke illustration of EVENET supporting multiple analysis tasks.
Simulation-to-reality bridge linking simulated collision events with real detector data.
paper_title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
paper_authors: Ting-Hsiang Hsu, Baihong Zhou, Qibin Liu, Yue Xu, Shu Li
